findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm server-side Gerrit feature-branch + no-ff merge-back rights exist BEFORE committing to that mechanism; if they do not, adopt the direct-to-main sequential-landing approach (each story individually reviewed/Verified, landed in dependency order) as the plan of record and rewrite AC10-13 to attest per-story landing rather than a merge-back change.
evidence: Approach: 'Deliver independently reviewed stories into a short-lived Gerrit feature branch, then merge the completed branch atomically to main.'
AC10-13 all reference 'The final no-ff merge-back change'.

Epic completion comment: 'MERGE-BACK (AC10-13): N/A — no server-side feature branch was used. Per the Codex Gerrit workflow rule (feature-branch-driver rights unavailable), each story was landed as an independent, individually-reviewed change directly to main in dependency order'
findings.finding: The Approach hardwires a mechanism — 'a short-lived Gerrit feature branch, then merge the completed branch atomically to main' with a 'final no-ff merge-back change' (AC10-13) — without establishing that server-side feature-branch creation/merge-back rights are available in this Gerrit workflow. The epic completion comment states this capability was in fact unavailable ('feature-branch-driver rights unavailable') and stories were landed directly to main instead, so 4 ACs (AC10-13) were marked N/A. The plan's chosen mechanism was not the best-fit for the actual environment.
findings.location: Approach section ('short-lived Gerrit feature branch, then merge the completed branch atomically to main') and Acceptance Criteria AC10-AC13 (the 'final no-ff merge-back change').
scenarios: Implementer follows the plan literally, attempts to create/merge a server-side feature branch, and is blocked by missing Gerrit rights — forcing an unplanned pivot to direct-to-main landing mid-execution.
AC10-13 become unsatisfiable-as-written and must be waived (as the completion comment did), leaving the epic's atomicity guarantee unverified against the criteria as stated.

findings.finding: AC #1's verification command `rebar list-descendants facb-44c3-2ada-41ee --output json reports no open or in_progress direct child` names a CLI capability the command does not have: `list-descendants` takes only `<root_ticket_id>` (no `--output json` flag — it is silently ignored), emits a BFS of ALL descendants bucketed by TYPE as ticket-ID strings with NO status field, and does not distinguish DIRECT children — so it cannot report 'no open or in_progress direct child.'
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC #1 ('Every direct child is closed; rebar list-descendants … --output json reports no open or in_progress direct child.')
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC #1 recipe with: 'Every direct child is closed; `rebar list --parent=facb-44c3-2ada-41ee --status=open,in_progress --output json` returns an empty array.' (`--parent` = direct children; `--status` filters lifecycle state.)
